feed.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
feed.subtitle: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

entry.title: Investigation continues into whether U.K. air base incident is linked to Iran
entry.summary: Questions continue to swirl around a U.K. military base and potential Iran-backed attacks.

entry.title: Security expert explains why Iran would target an U.K. air base
entry.summary: NPR's A Martínez asks Megan Sutcliffe, who focuses on security risks in the Middle East, why Iran would want to target a British air base.

entry.title: Trump hits the road to campaign for GOP candidates ahead of the midterm elections
entry.summary: President Trump hits the campaign trail as Republicans look to rally turnout ahead of the midterms.

entry.title: 5 things civil rights data says about public schools
entry.summary: The federal Civil Rights Data Collection, for the first time in decades, tells us about the teacher workforce and reminds us racial disparities are still stark in American public schools.

entry.title: Carpetbagger allegation, misplaced valor make Nevada's safe red House seat competitive
entry.summary: Northern Nevada has a reliably red congressional seat, represented by a Republican since it was drawn in the early 1980s. A complicated candidate and a potential blue wave this year could change that.

entry.title: BTS frontman RM is showing his art collection. Fans are flocking to see it
entry.summary: The pop superstar is showing art from his personal collection for the first time. The San Francisco Museum of Modern Art is packed with fans.

entry.title: Morning news brief
entry.summary: The investigation continues into whether Iran is linked it an incident at a U.K. air base, thousands join student-led protest in France, former German spy chief to face charges including espionage.

entry.title: Podcaster Jennifer Welch talks about her new book, 'Not Today, Fascists'
entry.summary: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with podcaster Jennifer Welch about her new book, "Not Today, Fascists."

entry.title: Cornell students plan sit-in to protest handling of former student's rape allegations
entry.summary: Former U.S. Deputy Attorney General Sally Yates will lead an independent inquiry into Cornell's handling of a former student's rape allegations. Students are preparing for a sit-in Wednesday.

entry.title: Former Tennessee prisons chief also oversaw botched executions in Arizona
entry.summary: Before Tennessee's prisons chief stepped down in the aftermath of a horrific failed execution, he oversaw botched executions in Arizona. A review of protocols there spelled out serious issues.
